en: Never leave an aerosol spray can in a hot car because heating the gas inside increases pressure and can cause the can to explode.
You must shake liquid antibiotic suspensions before use because the solid medicine particles settle at the bottom of the liquid mixture over time.
Never mix bleach with ammonia because combining these two liquids causes a dangerous chemical change that releases toxic chlorine gas into the air.
Wooden spoons are safer than metal spoons for stirring hot soup because wood is a thermal insulator that does not conduct heat to your hand.
Never touch dry ice with bare hands because its extremely low temperature causes solid carbon dioxide to rapidly absorb heat and freeze your skin.
Soap helps wash greasy dishes because its molecules act as an emulsifier, allowing water and oil to mix so the grease rinses away cleanly.
Squeezing lemon juice on sliced apples prevents browning because the citric acid slows the chemical change occurring when fruit enzymes react with oxygen.
Keep rubbing alcohol away from open flames because it is highly flammable and its liquid state quickly evaporates into a gas that easily ignites.
Adding a pinch of salt and sugar to water creates an electrolyte solution that helps your body absorb fluids faster when dehydrated from sweating.
Pouring boiling water into a cold glass pitcher causes a rapid physical change in temperature that makes the brittle solid glass crack and shatter.
Sweating cools your body because the liquid water on your skin absorbs heat to evaporate into a gas, taking that thermal energy away.
Flour dust suspended in the air is highly explosive because breaking the solid into tiny particles vastly increases its surface area for rapid combustion.
